unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U17: Keep small-company classification separate from stale thresholds and MSME status

payload.title: A familiar label can have a versioned legal definition
payload.core_explanation_md:
Small company is a Companies Act classification with financial criteria and exclusions. It is not automatically the same as a small enterprise under MSME classification. The textbook financial limits and its either/or wording must not be treated as current reference data. Check both prescribed financial criteria and the statutory exclusions for the relevant date before using a relaxation.

Record the paid-up capital, the relevant financial-year turnover, the legal form and any holding/subsidiary or other excluded status. A claim of smallness based only on staff count or loan size is insufficient. The applicable prescribed thresholds need primary-notification reconciliation before the release question bank tests an exact current limit.

self_check.prompt_text: Can MSME registration alone establish small-company status?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. These are different legal classifications.

payload.stem_md: A company seeks a small-company compliance relaxation solely because it has an MSME certificate. What is needed?

options.explanation_md: It does not prove the Companies Act classification.

options.text_md: A rule that all MSMEs are companies

options.explanation_md: That is not the complete classification test.

options.text_md: The applicable Companies Act criteria, exclusions and dated prescribed limits
options.explanation_md: The two classifications must be assessed separately.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The two classifications must be assessed separately.

payload.stem_md: An old textbook threshold conflicts with a later prescription before the exam cutoff. Which evidence should control authoring?

options.text_md: The applicable dated primary prescription, with the conflict recorded

options.explanation_md: No legal basis supports averaging thresholds.
